Memory — Metaphysical Gaps (Five Vignettes)

Five metaphysical threads that complement the concepts of emptiness, field ontologies, observer participation, information conservation, and emergent mind.

  • Time: Memory as a generator of causal order (retrocausality/process perspectives).
  • Unity: Recollection as the many returning to the One (Neoplatonism) and as latent “seeds” in ālayavijñāna (Yogācāra).
  • Ethics: Remembering-as-re-membering — mnemonic ecology.
  • Potential: Memory as stored capacity (dunamis) and durée.
  • Logos: Memory as the universe’s self-organizing record.

Memory and Causality Beyond Time

Memory doesn’t merely follow causality; it can be the structure by which temporal order coheres. Process philosophy treats moments as “prehending” one another, integrating the universe’s available data into new unities. Retrocausal models in quantum theory explore whether present observations can constrain or “select” past-consistent histories.

  • Why it matters: Situates recall inside a bidirectional temporality; complements constructive episodic simulation and temporal context models.
  • Pointers: Whitehead’s “actual occasions” and “prehensions”; retrocausality (Cramer; SEP overview).

Memory and the One / Monad

In Neoplatonism, the One emanates Nous and Soul; recollection is a movement from multiplicity back toward unity. In Yogācāra, ālayavijñāna is a latent “storehouse” stream carrying seeds (bīja) that condition experience; “remembering” activates patterned potentials.

  • Why it matters: Bridges Western emanationist metaphysics with Eastern accounts of latent continuity.
  • Pointers: Plotinus on emanation; Yogācāra on seeds and transformations of consciousness.

Mnemonic Ethics & Ecology

If memory is what maintains relational continuity, ethics becomes the care of memory—restoring, preserving, and renewing ties across persons and ecologies. “To re-member” is literally to bring members back into relation.

Memory and the Metaphysics of Potential

Beyond storing the actual, memory is a reservoir of potential—Aristotelian dunamis awaiting energeia, resonant with Bergson’s durée where past coexists with the present as a virtual field guiding action.

Memory as Self‑Organizing Logos

In Stoic and allied traditions, Logos names the rational principle immanent in nature. Read informationally, memory can be seen as the universe’s logos-function: a recursive ordering that records, constrains, and enables new formations—echoing “it from bit” and participatory cosmology.
